stemMd: Why is energy typically lower at higher trophic levels in a food chain?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Matter disappears whenever an animal feeds.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Decomposers convert all heat back into usable food energy.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Organisms use energy in metabolism and release much of it as heat before it can be transferred.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Every consumer creates energy from nothing.

explanationMd: Only part of the chemical energy taken in becomes biomass available to the next trophic level. Much supports metabolism and is dissipated as heat, while some material is not eaten or assimilated. Energy flows through ecosystems; it does not cycle in the same way as nutrient atoms.

distractorRationale.e: Energy is conserved and cannot be created by consumers.
distractorRationale.b: Heat is not fully recycled into food-chain chemical energy.
distractorRationale.a: Matter is transformed and recycled, not destroyed by feeding.
distractorRationale.c: Consumers and decomposers also carry out energy-releasing metabolism.
